input.summary: The original recorded data are unavailable, so reanalysis is not feasible. Instead, a bounded emulated-netem-v1 pilot is proposed to test whether adding 20 ms one-way delay changes TCP flow completion time under fixed bottleneck conditions. Three unresolved questions remain about delay placement, directionality, and file size, so protocol is null pending owner clarification.
questions: Is the 20 ms delay applied one-way or round-trip (i.e., is it added to one client's path or symmetrically to both directions)?
What file size(s) in MB should be used for the TCP flows to match the paper's intended conditions?
Which TCP congestion control algorithm(s) (e.g., cubic, bbr, reno) were used in the original claim's emulated setup?

proposal.problem: The original recorded data for this synthetic networking claim are unavailable, making direct reanalysis impossible. A new emulated measurement is needed to assess whether adding 20 ms delay changes TCP flow completion time under fixed bottleneck conditions.
proposal.question: Does adding 20 ms of emulated delay to a TCP flow's path change its flow completion time under fixed bottleneck conditions, compared to a baseline with no added delay?
proposal.hypothesis: Under fixed emulated bottleneck conditions, adding 20 ms delay changes TCP flow completion time.
proposal.conditions: Two conditions are compared: (1) baseline — no added delay; (2) treatment — 20 ms delay added to the client path. Bottleneck rate and buffer size are held fixed across both conditions. Delay placement (one-way vs. round-trip), file size, and CCA remain unresolved and must be confirmed before freezing the protocol.
proposal.related_work: No full text or cited prior work was provided with this claim. The claim is described as synthetic and retrieved-unreviewed; no independent citations are introduced here.
proposal.alternatives: Alternative explanations for any observed difference include: (a) increased retransmission due to higher RTT inflating completion time; (b) slow-start prolongation under higher RTT; (c) buffer bloat interactions at the bottleneck. These mechanisms are untested alternatives and are not asserted.
proposal.design: A new emulated measurement using the netem-v1 runner is proposed, comparing flow completion time (ms) between a no-delay control and a 20 ms delay treatment across matched TCP flows. This is a new-measurement independent check, not a reanalysis of unavailable original data.
proposal.metrics: Primary metric: flow_completion_time_ms (ms). Success criterion: a detectable difference in median completion time between the 0 ms and 20 ms delay conditions across replications.
proposal.controls: Bottleneck rate (Mbit/s), bottleneck buffer size (kbytes), file size (MBytes), CCA, and number of clients are held constant across conditions. Only the client delay parameter varies.
proposal.falsification: The claim is falsified if flow completion time distributions under 0 ms and 20 ms delay are indistinguishable (e.g., overlapping medians and interquartile ranges across all replications), suggesting the 20 ms delay has no detectable effect under these conditions.
proposal.inputs: No original data, code, or versioned artifacts were supplied. The source SHA256 (aaaa...aaaa) and packet SHA256 (a1b4...0da) are retained from the claim packet. Delay placement, file size, and CCA are unresolved inputs that must be provided by the owner.
proposal.limitations: The original data are unavailable; this is a new independent measurement, not a reanalysis. The claim is synthetic and unreviewed. Delay directionality, file size, and CCA are unknown, preventing a complete protocol. A pilot cannot establish causality or generalize beyond the tested configuration.
